policy.seeding: Seed every ceiling from at least 3 clean release-style runs on fresh hosted runners. Take a robust upper bound over the per-run median-of-round p95 values and multiply by a justified headroom factor. Never seed from a single run plus an arbitrary percentage.
policy.increases: A budget increase requires a dedicated reviewed change recording the affected benchmark, old and new ceilings, the repeated raw measurements, the cause and user impact, the alternatives considered, and why optimization or rollback is not appropriate.
policy.decreases: Ceilings may ratchet down to lock in a proven improvement once repeated measurements support the lower value.
policy.automation: No task, script, or workflow may write this file. A breach blocks the release; it never updates the budget.
policy.environment: Ceilings are only valid on the canonical target, Node version and runner image family. Drift in any of those three is a recalibration failure, not a comparison. runnerImageVersions records the exact image builds the ceilings were seeded on. A run on a different build is reported as a diagnostic and does not block, for the same reason the CPU model does not block: GitHub chooses the machine, it rebuilds the image about every week, and releases are less frequent than that. The headroom over observedUpperMs covers that variation. CPU model is reported as a diagnostic too — spread the seeding runs across the models that appear.
